title: kv-cache: tune eviction/defrag heuristics to reduce spillover and fragmentation
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: In high-concurrency serving workloads we observed increased KV cache spillover and fragmentation under long-tail sequence length distributions. Spillover increases host-side paging and degrades throughput for concurrent in-flight requests. This PR introduces a set of coordinated heuristic changes to eviction scoring, fragmentation tracking, adaptive compaction windows, and spillover backpressure to reduce total spillover bytes and improve steady-state memory utilization.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces a new eviction_score that combines recency, size, and fragmentation_penalty to prefer compact, large entries for eviction.
- Tracks per-slab fragmentation metrics and exposes "fragmentation_ratio" counters to the runtime for smarter decisions.
- Adds an adaptive_compaction window: when fragmentation_ratio for a slab exceeds a threshold we compact proactively instead of waiting for full eviction.
- Implements spillover_backpressure in the scheduler: when device memory pressure is high, new KV insertions are rate-limited and compressed candidates are preferred.
- Adds unit and benchmark tests, and a short docs entry describing heuristic knobs.

Design notes:
- Eviction score is computed as: score = alpha*LRU_age + beta*(size_bytes) + gamma*(fragmentation_penalty). alpha/beta/gamma are runtime-configurable. We default to alpha=1, beta=0.8, gamma=1.5 after tuning against the microbenchmarks.
- Fragmentation_penalty is a lightweight estimate (free_slots/total_slots) per slab; we avoid full defragmentation during hot paths.
- Adaptive compaction runs opportunistically with a capped CPU budget (percent of core cycles) to avoid stealing cycles from inference.

Testing and results:
- Benchmarks (local perf infra) across realistic request traces show spillover bytes reduced by ~48% at 95th percentile load, tail p99 latency unaffected (+/- <1%), and a net 6% increase in throughput under stress tests with mixed sequence lengths.
- All unit tests and integration benches added to CI. Initial bench job failed due to a flaky compaction race; fixed by adding a lightweight CAS in the compactor.

Rollout plan:
- Canary deploy to Dedicated pools (~5% traffic) for 48 hours, observe spillover, memory pressure, and latency.
- Increase to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if no regressions.
- Expose alpha/beta/gamma and fragmentation thresholds as runtime flags for quick rollback/tuning.

Checklist:
- [x] Eviction scoring implementation and config parsing
- [x] Fragmentation tracking counters + metrics export
- [x] Adaptive compaction implementation with CPU cap
- [x] Spillover backpressure in scheduler
- [x] Unit tests + benches
- [x] Docs update (docs/kv-eviction.md)

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the compaction code path and the CAS added to avoid races when two threads attempt compaction on the same slab. The compaction is best-effort and non-blocking w.r.t. serving fastpath.

Related: previous work on spillover-defrag heuristics (see PRs pr-272846, pr-296112, pr-341500).

review_comments: Marcus Li: Can you explain the default alpha/beta/gamma values and how sensitive perf is to them? Suggest adding an integration test that validates no p99 regression at default knobs.

Aisha Khan: Added integration bench and sensitivity sweep to benchmarks/kv_spillover_bench.rs; results included in PR description. Default knobs chosen from the sweep; we also make them runtime-configurable for quick tuning.
Priya Patel: The compaction CAS looks fine but please ensure the flag is cleared on early returns and on panic paths. Also add a metric for compaction CPU time.
Aisha Khan: Added RAII guard to clear flag and added compaction_cpu_ms metric (exported via runtime metrics).
Sofia Berg: I saw the initial bench fail on CI due to a race; can you summarize the fix?
Aisha Khan: The fix was to serialize compaction start using the CAS + RAII guard and to avoid triggering compaction while the slab is being resized. I re-ran the bench job and it passed.
ci_checks: benchmarks: pass (initial run failed; rerun after race fix passed)

release_notes:
- Reduce KV cache spillover by ~48% at 95th percentile workload
- Add tunable eviction scoring (LRU+size+fragmentation)
- Add adaptive compaction and spillover backpressure to improve memory utilization
- Expose runtime knobs for rapid tuning/rollback
rollout_plan: Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics monitoring (spillover_bytes, fragmentation_ratio, p99 latency). Runtime flags available for immediate rollback.
notes: This is safe to backport to the latest maintenance branches if customers report high spillover; flagged as backport-candidate.
